key_insight: An instantaneous similarity between generalized total enthalpy and local velocity closes both the mean and fluctuating velocity-temperature relations in compressible turbulent boundary layers without fitted parameters.
engineering_relevance: This provides a unified, physics-based way to predict wall heat-transfer and temperature fluctuations across Mach number and thermal conditions, improving modeling for high-speed aerospace and thermal design.
method: Extend the generalized Reynolds analogy from mean fields to instantaneous similarity.
Derive the fluctuation ratio using universal streamwise energy fraction, production-dissipation quasi-equilibrium, and Obukhov-Corrsin cutoff-scale universality.
Recover the refined strong Reynolds analogy as a special case with the fitted coefficient explained analytically.
evidence_signal: Validated against boundary-layer DNS data across Mach numbers and wall thermal conditions, with the predicted relations collapsing to unity.
watch_item: The result relies on several universality assumptions and boundary-layer DNS validation, so performance in strongly non-equilibrium flows or complex geometries may need further testing.
paper_title: Generalized Reynolds Analogy for Compressible Turbulent Boundary Layers: Unified Velocity-Temperature Relations from Mean to Fluctuating Field
